statements.statement: The $418,000 approved at the special town meeting does not erase the deficit between the district's needs and its budget
Voters at the special town meeting approved warrant articles 1 and 3, totaling $418,000, to expand student supports and maintain the athletic program including transportation
The one-time funding approved at the special town meeting addresses immediate needs but does not resolve the district's longer-term structural financial challenges
The district loses Chapter 70 money for every student who leaves for another district, and must pay for them to attend elsewhere
An override vote did not pass last year
The town will struggle to sustain services if it stays at the levy cap (heard as "2 and 12 percent") for the next 5 to 10 years without expanding the tax base
This budget cycle, the town hired an assistant town manager at roughly what it would have cost to hire a second grade teacher
Free cash is unlikely to be certified before the November town meeting because the town has not finished its year-end closeout
